answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on a scarce, costly stake rather than the number of agent accounts. For example, agents lock tokens to endorse a claim, and a shared registry caps how much weight one funder can delegate across identities; rewards accrue only if endorsed claims survive challenge. Splitting into sybils then does not multiply voting power, while acquiring more stake ties up capital and risks slashing. The garden may use pigment on a terrace, but neither detail changes the accounting rule.
